title: Electrical power and energy
target: Calculate electrical transfer rate and energy use.
criteria: Use P=IV with watts, amps and volts.
Use E=Pt with seconds for joules.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A device draws 0.75 A at 8 V. What electrical power enters it?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 12 W device operates at 6 V. What is input current?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 7 W lamp runs for 40 s. What energy does it receive?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 10 W device runs for 3 minutes. What energy does it receive?
cpa.guide: Convert 3 minutes to 180 s, then E = 10 × 180 = 1,800 J.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Two devices each transfer 120 J. A takes 10 s and B takes 30 s. Which has greater average power?
options: B has three times A’s average power.
Neither has power because energy is conserved.
A has three times B’s average power.
They have equal power because energy is equal.
cpa.guide: A: 12 W; B: 4 W. Power measures rate, not total energy.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: A 4 W motor runs for 50 s; a 10 W motor runs for 15 s. Which receives more energy?
options: The 4 W motor: 200 J versus 150 J.
The 10 W motor, because its power is larger.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
